checks.name: Stationarity of the surviving action in P1485 (10)
checks.assumptions: Treat q=x-dot squared and m as positive constants at a parameter value, and lambda>0. This comparison does not recover the cancelled sign or assume an unwritten measure factor.
derivation: For f(lambda)=q/lambda+m lambda, f-prime=-q/lambda^2+m and f-double-prime=2q/lambda^3>0. Stationarity gives lambda^2=q/m and f at that point is 2 sqrt(m q).

To obtain the separately written lambda^2=q/m^2, a different coefficient such as m^2 lambda would be needed. Even that choice gives 2m sqrt(q), so an additional factor 1/2 would be needed to give m times length. These are possible modified expressions, not decipherments.
checks.result: The surviving m lambda, the source denominator m^2 and exp(+mL) are all retained without adding m, 1/2 or a minus sign.

checks.name: The last differential in P1485 (11)
checks.assumptions: If x is a scalar differentiable function of t, dx=x-dot dt. The manuscript also uses vector-valued x elsewhere, so a bare dx can require additional interpretation.
derivation: The parameter-length expression is integral sqrt(x-dot squared) dt. Replacing dt by dx would instead give integral sqrt(x-dot squared) x-dot dt in the scalar case.
For x(t)=2t on [0,1], the two ordinary scalar integrals are 2 and 4. Thus the differential cannot be changed as mere typography.
checks.result: Visual dx remains in the diplomatic text with dt as a reading alternative. Parameter invariance does not decipher the last letter.

checks.name: An explicitly convergent interpretation of the integral in P1485 (12)
checks.assumptions: For this comparison only, take lambda on (0,infinity), a=-A, b=-B and A,B>0. The source supplies no contour, limits or sign conditions.
derivation: Substitute lambda=sqrt(B/A) exp(u), so d lambda/lambda=du and A lambda+B/lambda=2 sqrt(AB) cosh(u). The resulting integral on the real u-axis is twice the integral from 0 to infinity of exp(-2 sqrt(AB) cosh(u)) du.
Using DLMF 10.32.9 at nu=0, this equals 2 K_0(2 sqrt(AB)). If instead a,b>0 on the same positive-real contour, the integral diverges at both ends.
checks.result: The written exp(sqrt(ab)) is not established by either real-contour example. No Bessel function, contour or normalization replaces the literal formula.

checks.name: The KPZ radicand and the four source sample dimensions
checks.assumptions: Use the principal nonnegative real square root in the displayed algebraic expression; this is not a claim about a physical branch or a proof of the KPZ theorem.
derivation: The radicand (D-1)(D-25) is nonnegative exactly for D<=1 or D>=25. At 25 it is zero; 26 is not this polynomial boundary.
Direct rational evaluation gives gamma(-2)=-1, gamma(0)=-1/2, gamma(1/2)=-1/3 and gamma(1)=0.
checks.result: The source sentence with “and” and 26 is retained. Algebra alone does not explain its intended restriction.

checks.name: Asymptotics of the retained factorial quotient in P1487 (8)
checks.assumptions: Let k tend to positive infinity and initially omit the separately ambiguous factor 9^k/g^k. Compare the literal quotient, without identifying boundary-rooted and spherical graph conventions.
derivation: Write a_k=2 Gamma(4k-2)/(Gamma(3k) Gamma(k+1)). Stirling expansion yields a_k asymptotic to [sqrt(3)/(16 sqrt(2 pi))] (256/27)^k k^(-5/2). The k power is (4k-5/2)-(3k-1/2)-(k+1/2)=-5/2.

The source (7) with gamma=-1/2 has power -7/2. A change of marked-vertex or boundary convention can introduce a factor proportional to k; the two counts are not identified by this calculation. A literal 9^k would multiply the exponential base by 9, while a formal g^k could have another role. Neither observation determines the glyph.
checks.result: The cancelled fraction, retained quotient, source asymptotic and both factor candidates remain unchanged.

checks.name: Gaussian graph integrals and the inner-vertex qualification in P1488
checks.assumptions: Use each undirected edge once, D independent Euclidean coordinates and ordinary Lebesgue measures. The source measure normalization is unspecified. Its separate words “inner vertices” can mean a fixed outer boundary.
derivation: For a closed trivalent graph, the edge action is x^T L x with L=3I-G. Each row sums to zero, so translations give a zero mode and the ordinary unpinned Gaussian integral is divergent.

With boundary values b fixed, write the inner action x^T L_II x-2x^T c+s_B. If L_II is positive definite, completing the square gives pi^(ND/2) det(L_II)^(-D/2) times exp(-s_B+c^T L_II^(-1)c), separately in each target coordinate.

For K4 the full L=4I-J has determinant 0. Pin one vertex at zero; the 3 by 3 minor has determinant 16, and its D=1 integral is pi^(3/2)/4. Thus inner vertices and boundary data matter, and the closed-graph counterexample cannot simply be applied to every version of (9).
checks.result: The source determinant formula is preserved. A normalization and treatment of boundary values or zero modes would be needed to make the equality precise.

checks.name: Exterior multiplication and exactness of the full exterior module
checks.assumptions: Work over a field with v nonzero, and choose a linear functional ell with ell(v)=1. The exact computation uses dimension 4, v=(1,2,0,-1), ell=e_1 dual.
derivation: Exterior multiplication d_v=v wedge satisfies d_v^2=0. The contraction identity i_ell(v wedge alpha)+v wedge i_ell(alpha)=ell(v) alpha=alpha gives a contracting homotopy.

Consequently ker(d_v)=im(d_v) for the full exterior algebra at every nonzero v. The program verifies both identities on all 16 exterior-basis elements with exact rational coefficients. General identity follows by the contraction rule.
checks.result: The source example of the zero bundle for the full exterior module is consistent with this fiberwise calculation.

checks.name: The truncated-algebra example and its written twist
checks.assumptions: Interpret the displayed kernel literally as a subbundle of the trivial bundle with fiber Lambda^k V on P(V), without an additional unstated twist or degree-shift convention.
derivation: For k=1, ker(v wedge: V -> Lambda^2 V)=Cv for each nonzero v. Over the space of lines this is the tautological O(-1). The source defines O(-1) this way on the preceding page.

The displayed right side for k=1 is Omega^0 tensor O(1)=O(1). On P^1, choose frames (1,z) and (w,1), with w=1/z. The latter is z^(-1) times the former, whereas the dual transitions have the inverse factor. The two literal line bundles therefore have opposite degree.
This isolates a mismatch under the stated untwisted interpretation. Regrading, dualizing or inserting twists is a possible change of construction, not source text.
checks.result: The written Omega^(k-1) tensor O(k) is retained. The calculation does not select an intended correction.

checks.name: The symplectic three-term module and the inserted “symm.”
checks.assumptions: Assume a nondegenerate alternating form on V in characteristic different from 2, as required by the source word “symplect.”. This assumption is not assigned to the inserted abbreviation.
derivation: The composition C -> V -> C is 1 -> v -> [v,v]=0 for an alternating form. The middle cohomology is v-perp/Cv.
Nondegeneracy gives (v-perp)-perp=Cv, so the radical of the form restricted to v-perp is Cv. Its quotient is nondegenerate and has dimension dimV-2.

For the symmetric identity form and v=e_1 the composition is 1, so a symmetric form does not define this complex for all projective v. It would require restricting to isotropic v or changing the setup.
checks.result: Both the symplectic wording and inserted symm. remain. The computation does not silently supply a missing skew- prefix.

checks.name: Clifford form normalization in P1490
checks.assumptions: Use characteristic different from 2 and treat h as the displayed degree-2 element. No diagonal value for the source pairing is assumed.
derivation: Putting v-prime=v in vv-prime+v-prime-v=<v,v-prime>h gives 2v^2=<v,v>h. Thus diagonal pairing 1 gives e_i^2=h/2, while diagonal pairing 2 gives the separately written e_i^2=h.
Off-diagonal pairing zero gives anticommutation of distinct basis vectors. The uncertain orthon./orthog. abbreviation does not independently establish the diagonal value.
checks.result: The two literal relations can agree at diagonal 2. The comparison therefore records a convention question rather than asserting an unconditional factor error.

checks.name: A precise quaternion comparison for r=3
checks.assumptions: For comparison only specialize to the real algebra with h=1 and e_i^2=+1. This does not interpret the source approximation sign or specify its field.
derivation: Anticommutation reduces products to 8 ordered monomials. The exact signed-XOR multiplication table on these 8 symbols is associative (all 512 triples checked), providing an 8-dimensional algebra realizing those relations.

Its even part has basis 1,e_1e_2,e_2e_3,e_1e_3. Set i=e_1e_2,j=e_2e_3,k=e_1e_3: all three square to -1 and ij=k,jk=i,ki=j, with reversed products negated. This even subalgebra has the quaternion multiplication table.

The full 8-dimensional algebra is not the 4-dimensional real quaternion algebra. The even-part comparison is a valid conditional reading of the nearby idea, not an expansion inserted into the manuscript.
checks.result: The source “approximately quaternions” remains verbatim in translation.

checks.name: The null-vector differential on the quadric
checks.assumptions: Characteristic different from 2; use the literal Clifford relation and a vector with <v,v>=0.
derivation: The literal relation gives 2v^2=<v,v>h=0, hence v^2=0. Multiplication by v therefore squares to zero on any graded module.
For non-isotropic vectors this conclusion need not hold. The restriction to the quadric matters; no claimed general classification theorem is proved by this elementary calculation.
checks.result: The null-vector construction is consistent under these assumptions; the source theorem remains a historical assertion, not certified here.
